doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Closing, a planned musical and goodbyes
summary: Final remarks on Merrill reissues, a musical he is writing, and wrapping up.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: them reissued here. It seems to be not easy. But we’re hoping, soon. Those records I’ll stand on.
Well you’ve had an amazing run at it, and you’re still doing it.
Yeah still doing it, you know not as often but not that much work. See if I left out any big thing. I probably have but—
Well we could do part two down the road, all right?
If you have some other things to talk about.
For the last several years I’ve been writing a musical with a guy.
All right. Well I hope I see it on Broadway.
We do too. I’m not a Broadway person but he asked me, this guy, he writes for the New York Times his name is Barry Singer.
All right. Well this has been fascinating for me. I really appreciate your coming and thanks for your time.
It’s been fun. Yeah. I probably editorialized too much.
No I don’t think so. I love some of the stuff you were saying and we really probably could do another session.
Yeah, is there any chance that I could hear what I wanted out of this?
